themes.name: Integration of Education for Sustainable Development into Curricula
themes.definition: This theme involves embedding principles of sustainability and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) into university courses and programs across various disciplines, often through curriculum design and alignment efforts.
evidence: [AhmCoD_2023] the CoDesignS ESD Framework (hereafter 'Framework') focused on HEIs, though the Framework is applicable to other types of educational institutions.
[PriEna_2024] a whole-institution approach to embedding education for sustainable development (ESD) in curricula.
[BalCon_2025] an innovative educational approach, applicable in various university contexts, which involves the analysis of interdependencies between SDG 2: Zero Hunger and the other SDGs.

themes.name: Pedagogical Approaches for Sustainability Education
themes.definition: This theme focuses on specific teaching methods and learning environments used to deliver sustainability education, including active learning strategies, problem-based learning, and game-based approaches.
evidence: [MarPed_2021] Pedagogical tools, such as problem-based learning (PBL) or research-based learning (RBL), and environmental tools, such as the life cycle assessment (LCA) and computational thinking (CT), have been used.
[YeuCom_2017] comparing pedagogies for plastic waste management at university level.
[CzoLea_2023] Learning Effects of Augmented Reality and Game-Based Learning for Science Teaching in Higher Education in the Context of Education for Sustainable Development.

themes.name: Development of Sustainability Competencies and Outcomes
themes.definition: This theme centers on the acquisition of knowledge, skills, attitudes, and behaviors related to sustainability among students, including competencies for leadership, activism, and pro-environmental actions.
evidence: [DloCom_2019] Competences to Address SDGs in Higher Education-A Reflection on the Equilibrium between Systemic and Personal Approaches to Achieve Transformative Action.

[SheSee_2015] sustainability attributes may be described in terms of knowledge, skills and competencies but that these are underpinned by affective attributes such as values, attitudes and dispositions.
[HenAn _2022] systems thinking and futures thinking are key learning outcomes related to students’ climate change leadership development and activism.

themes.name: Institutional and Collaborative Strategies for ESD
themes.definition: This theme involves university-level policies, partnerships, and collaborative efforts to implement Education for Sustainable Development, including external collaborations with industry, government, or other institutions.
evidence: [MagLev_2025] Leveraging educational partnerships to integrate education for sustainable development into university geoscience curriculum.
[PriSup_2021] supporting the role of universities in leading individual and societal transformation through education for sustainable development.
[B. Hig_2019] higher education for sustainable development: actioning the global goals in policy, curriculum and practice.

themes.name: Experiential and Real-World Learning in Sustainability
themes.definition: This theme emphasizes hands-on, practical learning experiences that connect sustainability education to real-world contexts, such as laboratories, field studies, community projects, and professional applications.
evidence: [LorInn_2022] Real-World Laboratory 'Ackerbaum'—an agroforestry system

[SimUni_2021] marine science professional development program to expose undergraduate students to ocean literacy principles and climate change concepts through marine ecology research and educational outreach.
[HunRef_2023] a reflective and cooperative learning approach to science, technology, engineering, arts, and math (STEAM) education. A case study examined Wanluan Township

themes.name: Climate Change and Environmental Literacy Education
themes.definition: This theme focuses specifically on educating students about climate change, environmental issues, and related literacy, often linked to Sustainable Development Goals like SDG 13 (Climate Action).
evidence: [GupEff_2025] solutions-based climate education
[ElsFos_2025] Fostering Sustainability Leadership Through SDG 13 Integration in Business Curricula
[SenA c_2021] MOOC-based climate change education

themes.name: Use of Technology in Sustainability Education
themes.definition: This theme involves the application of digital tools, online platforms, augmented reality, and other technologies to enhance learning and engagement in sustainability education.
evidence: [ÁlvDev_2018] Developing digital educational materials for nursing and sustainability
[CzoLea_2023] augmented reality (AR) and game-based learning
[PerTow_2021] Towards effective e-learning on sustainability: a case study-course on participatory processes in environmental politics

data.meta_observations: The abstracts consistently emphasize Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) as central frameworks. There is a strong focus on pedagogical diversity, student outcomes, and institutional integration, with recurring mentions of experiential learning and technology use. Many abstracts report on case studies or specific interventions, but some lack detailed methodological or quantitative data, as noted in quality warnings.
data.grounding_notes: All themes are derived from explicit terminology and concepts in the abstracts, with verbatim evidence provided. However, some abstracts have missing elements (e.g., objectives, methods, conclusions), which limits the depth of evidence for certain themes. No inferences were made beyond the stated text. Frequency is assessed based on the number of articles in this batch that directly mention the theme, with 'Medium' indicating several articles per theme.
